AFDLSX

Area Forecast Discussion
National Weather Service St Louis MO
602 PM CDT Thu Oct 8 2026

.KEY MESSAGES...

- Near-record warmth and predominantly dry weather is forecast into 
  early next week. 

- The remnants of Tropical Cyclone Isaias bring slightly
  "cooler" temperatures Saturday and Sunday due to clouds, as
  well as chances of light rain in southeast Missouri and
  southwest Illinois.

&&

.SHORT TERM /THROUGH FRIDAY NIGHT/...
Issued at 232 PM CDT Thu Oct 8 2026

Another mostly clear night is forecast across the area, with 
exception of parts of northeast Missouri and west-central 
Illinois where an increase in midlevel clouds is expected. The 
combination of a clear sky, light/variable winds, and seasonably
low dewpoints (~25th percentile) will promote favorable 
conditions for radiational cooling across much of the area. 
This is especially true across southeast Missouri into southwest
and south-central Illinois near the surface ridge axis. 
Guidance for several days has had a distinct warm bias, and this
should continue tonight in those aforementioned areas. Lows in 
the upper 40s to low 50s are forecast in these regions, with 
readings moderating into the mid 50s to low 60s as you travel 
northwestward. 

All remains on track for unseasonably warm temperatures again on 
Friday with the mid/upper level ridge amplifying across the 
region and 850-hPa temperatures climbing back above +18C (~99th
percentile of climatology). Plenty of sunshine is also 
expected, which will also help temperatures warm efficiently. 
Highs are forecast to be mostly in the mid to upper 80s, though
a few spots may top out right near 90 degrees. Daily records 
may be threatened at both St. Louis (89F/1938) and Columbia 
(91F/1893), with Quincy likely coming up at least a few degrees 
short (89F/1938). 

Milder low temperatures are forecast Friday night as mid/upper level 
clouds begin to increase after midnight in advance of the remnants 
of Hurricane Isaias. If these clouds are a bit later than forecast 
though, parts of southeast Missouri into south-central Illinois 
again may be cooler than forecast. Southerly winds are expected to 
be very light in those areas, particularly in river valleys where 
winds tend to decouple easier.

&&

.LONG TERM /SATURDAY THROUGH THURSDAY/...
Issued at 232 PM CDT Thu Oct 8 2026

(Saturday - Sunday)

The remnants of Hurricane Isaias have shifted slightly east across 
the Tennessee Valley this weekend. Consequently, the chances for a 
widespread, soaking rainfall have dropped across our southeast 
Missouri and southwest Illinois counties. The exact track of the low 
looks to come down to internal dynamics, with individual vorticity 
maxima rotating cyclonically around the broader midlevel 
circulation. Predicting specific internal dynamics are near 
impossible 24+ hours out, so there still may be a wobble 
longitudinally. A farther west (east) track would increase 
(decrease) the chances of light rain. As alluded to above, the 
latest track from the National Hurricane Center is slightly east. 
Probabilities for 0.25+" and 0.50+" have dropped significantly 
on the latest LREF, now generally below 10-20%. In fact, 
chances for as low as 0.10" have fallen as low as 15-30% even 
along the southeastern CWA border. While some light rain still 
seems likely in southeast Missouri and southwest Illinois, a 
vast majority of the area will stay dry. There will be at least 
some thickening mid/high level clouds moving northward on 
Saturday. These clouds should "cool" temperatures this weekend 
back into the low to mid 80s for most locations. 


(Sunday Night - Monday Night)

After a brief lull in the near-record warmth due to cloud cover 
associated with the remnants of Hurricane Isaias, it looks to return 
on Monday. The air mass still appears to be more impressive compared 
to Friday, with 500-hPa heights from the NAEFS above the 95th 
percentile of climatology and 850-hPa temperatures close to +20C
(near record for the date). Surface winds also should turn more
out of the southwest, which is more favorable for downslope 
winds off of the Ozark Plateau. Daily record high temperatures 
certainly look to be in jeopardy, with even the monthly record 
in St. Louis (94F on 10/11/1963) potentially under threat. Low 
temperatures are also expected to be on the upswing due to 
increasing surface winds and more cloud cover (especially Monday
night). Readings are forecast to only drop back into the 60s 
each night for most locations.


(Tuesday - Next Thursday)

Forecast spread increases for mid week, mainly due to uncertainty 
with the evolution of a cold front. This boundary is likely to move 
through at least parts of the area on Tuesday before wavering back 
north as a warm front later in the week. Confidence in temperatures 
is quite low due to the wavering front and uncertainty in its 
exact location. The inter-quartile range from the NBM is around 
15 degrees each day, helping illustrate the high spread in high 
temperatures. Chances of showers (and some thunderstorms) also 
increases during this period as low-level moisture convergence 
strengthens along with multiple midlevel impulses moving along 
the crest of the ridge axis.

&&

.AVIATION /18Z TAFS THROUGH 00Z SATURDAY/...
Issued at 557 PM CDT Thu Oct 8 2026

Fog is expected again tonight in most locations outside of Mid-
Missouri. Here, winds of 5-6kts may be slightly too strong for
fog to persist. Added mention of IFR visibilities to KSUS and 
KCPS, though will likely need to upgrade to LIFR. Outside of
fog, dry and VFR conditions will prevail through the TAF period.

&&

.CLIMATE...
Issued at 219 PM CDT Wed Oct 7 2026

Record high temperatures are possible between Friday 10/9 and Monday 
10/12. Here are current records at each of our 3 official climate 
stations:

                    KSTL            KCOU            KUIN
Friday 10/9       89/1938         91/1893         89/1938           
Saturday 10/10    92/1963         92/1963         89/1963
Sunday 10/11      94/1963         89/1962         88/1962
Monday 10/12      90/2024         94/1899         88/1975

&&

.LSX WATCHES/WARNINGS/ADVISORIES...
MO...None.
IL...None.

&&

$$

SHORT TERM...Gosselin
LONG TERM...Gosselin
AVIATION...Jaja
CLIMATE...Gosselin
